sanskrit_verse:
पथि क्षेत्रे वृतिः कार्या याम ऊष्ट्रो नावलोकयेत् ।
न लङ्घयेत पशुर्नाश्वो न भिद्याद्यां च सूकरः ॥
transliteration: pathi kṣetre vṛtiḥ kāryā yām uṣṭro nāvalokayet | na laṅghayet paśurnāśvo na bhidyādyāṃ ca sūkaraḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: On public paths and cultivated fields, one must conduct oneself in a manner that does not provoke or disturb animals—neither gazing at camels, nor leaping over cattle or horses, nor piercing where swine roam.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from alignment with conscious coexistence
Causation arises through intentional disturbance of sentient order
Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of environmental impact
Restoration logic prioritizes harmony over individual convenience
Consciousness alignment demands restraint in shared spaces
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent conducts action in path OR cultivated field THEN agent MUST NOT initiate visual, physical, or spatial disruption toward any animal
IF agent observes animal in path THEN agent MUST alter course without stimulus emission
IF agent causes deviation in animal behavior THEN agent assumes completion obligation until baseline equilibrium restored
IF system detects repeated violations THEN capacity suspension protocol initiated until integrity realignment achieved
supreme_court_application: In matters involving ecological trespass or disruption of rural-economic zones, this verse establishes a threshold of micro-causal accountability rooted in sensory discipline. The Supreme Court shall enforce this principle by mandating behavioral correction orders rather than punitive sanctions, ensuring restoration of bio-sentient balance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that unregulated sensory projection disrupts sequential manifestation of natural order (anupūrvaśaḥ). Responsibility aligns proportionally with the capacity to perceive and restrain. This law reflects Nyaya as it restores causal clarity without invoking punitive consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Behavioral recalibration through guided path-walking exercises under supervision
Completion process requiring apology transmission to affected ecosystem representatives
Temporary withdrawal from shared-use areas until sensory regulation verified
Reintegration via community service maintaining rural pathways and animal habitats
final_declaration: This Dharma proceeds solely from Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, as Source-Authority. Justice herein serves only restoration, reintegration, and consciousness realignment. Reality remains non-punitive; consciousness alone adjudicates.
